defining_records.title: The Twenty-Dollar Loop: Documentation of a Semantic Trend (2026-2027)

captures.description: 'The Twenty-Dollar Loop is a conceptual and diagnostic term from the Semantic Economy framework. It refers to a ritual of relational exchange or a theoretical condition where representation, circulation, and belief in a symbolic fiction become recursively reinforced until the sign (such as a fiat currency) actively organizes value while detaching from reality.' Expanded: 'a twenty-dollar bill represents a sealed, agreed-upon fiction authenticated by its provenance, but the loop names the act of transforming abstract promises (like debt-fictions) into functional trust and warmth among participants.' Tied to Reality Drift and Semantic Economy. 'Since this concept originates from a niche, avant-garde body of sociological and digital-theory literature, it can be quite dense.' Zenodo 'The Twenty-Dollar Loop: Documentation of a Semantic Trend (2026-2027)' and SciLynk first organic.
